alt: A wide ink-and-wash drawing of the US Supreme Court building in magenta and white against a black sky, its columned portico and pediment towering over the steps, with the seated marble figures flanking the entrance. At the foot of the steps two tiny protesters hold signs reading EQUAL and RIGHTS, one of them also carrying a striped flag.

Hand-lettered white and magenta text fills the top half of a black square, above the same magenta drawing of the Supreme Court building with two small protesters holding EQUAL and RIGHTS signs on the steps.
text:
THE SUPREME COURT ANNOUNCED APRIL 22 THAT IT WILL REVIEW CASES INVOLVING GAY AND TRANSGENDER EMPLOYEES WHO SAY THEY FACED WORKPLACE DISCRIMINATION.

THE COURT'S RULINGS WILL DECIDE WHETHER LGBT AMERICANS ARE PROTECTED BY FEDERAL ANTI-DISCRIMINATION LAWS.

EQUAL RIGHTS

alt: A hand-drawn map of the United States on black, with each state filled in one of four shades from deep magenta to white according to a legend below it; most of the South, the Plains and the Mountain West are left white for no protections, while the West Coast, Southwest and Northeast are dark magenta. Hand-lettered white and magenta text sits above the map and a four-swatch key runs across the bottom.
text:
RIGHT NOW, MANY STATES DON'T HAVE LAWS PROHIBITING DISCRIMINATION BASED ON SEXUAL ORIENTATION AND GENDER IDENTITY.

PROHIBITS DISCRIMINATION BASED ON SEXUAL ORIENTATION AND GENDER IDENTITY
PROHIBITS DISCRIMINATION AGAINST PUBLIC EMPLOYEES BASED ON SEXUAL ORIENTATION AND GENDER IDENTITY
PROHIBITS DISCRIMINATION AGAINST PUBLIC EMPLOYEES BASED ON SEXUAL ORIENTATION ONLY
NO PROTECTIONS

alt: A magenta-and-white brush portrait of a woman with shoulder-length hair, rectangular glasses, a beaded necklace and a floral-print top, looking calmly at the viewer from the left side of a black square. Hand-lettered white and magenta text runs across the top, and a smaller magenta caption sits to the right of her shoulder.
text:
THE JUSTICES ARE SET TO HEAR THREE CASES: TWO INVOLVING INDIVIDUALS WHO SAID THEY WERE FIRED BECAUSE OF THEIR SEXUAL ORIENTATION AND ONE INVOLVING AN EMPLOYEE WHO WAS FIRED AFTER COMING OUT AS A TRANS WOMAN.

AIMEE STEPHENS, LEFT, WAS FIRED FROM HER JOB AT A FUNERAL HOME TWO WEEKS AFTER COMING OUT AS TRANS.

alt: A pale pink watercolor scroll with curled ends floats on a black background, filled with hand-lettered black statutory text, with a parenthetical credit lettered in white beneath it. Magenta and white hand lettering fills the space above the scroll.
text:
THE CORE QUESTION IS WHETHER TITLE VII OF THE CIVIL RIGHTS ACT OF 1964, WHICH BANS GENDER-BASED DISCRIMINATION, COVERS DISCRIMINATION BASED ON SEXUAL ORIENTATION OR GENDER IDENTITY.

IT SHALL BE AN UNLAWFUL EMPLOYMENT PRACTICE FOR AN EMPLOYER TO FAIL OR REFUSE TO HIRE OR TO DISCHARGE ANY INDIVIDUAL, OR OTHERWISE TO DISCRIMINATE AGAINST ANY INDIVIDUAL WITH RESPECT TO HIS COMPENSATION, TERMS, CONDITIONS, OR PRIVILEGES OF EMPLOYMENT, BECAUSE OF SUCH INDIVIDUAL'S RACE, COLOR, RELIGION, SEX, OR NATIONAL ORIGIN.

(EXCERPT FROM TITLE VII)

alt: A grayscale brush portrait of Barack Obama in a dark suit with a magenta tie, one hand raised open-palmed mid-gesture, set against black flecked with small magenta specks. A magenta ribbon banner across the bottom is lettered with his name, and hand-lettered white and magenta text fills the top.
text:
UNTIL RECENTLY, WE WERE SEEING PROGRESS: FEDERAL APPEALS COURTS IN CHICAGO, NEW YORK AND CINCINNATI HAVE RULED THAT GAY AND LESBIAN PEOPLE ARE ENTITLED TO PROTECTION, AND THE OBAMA ADMINISTRATION'S POLICY WAS TO TREAT LGBT DISCRIMINATION CLAIMS AS SEX DISCRIMINATION.

OBAMA

alt: A grayscale brush portrait of Jeff Sessions in a suit, mouth slightly open, holding up a pale pink sheet of paper covered in hand-lettered black text, against a black background. A magenta ribbon banner at the lower left carries his name, and white and magenta hand lettering fills the upper right.
text:
WHEN TRUMP WAS A PRESIDENTIAL CANDIDATE, HE CLAIMED NOT TO BE AGAINST LGBT RIGHTS. BUT IN 2017 THE TRUMP JUSTICE DEPARTMENT ISSUED A MEMO SAYING THEY WILL NO LONGER ARGUE THAT TRANSGENDER PEOPLE ARE PROTECTED AGAINST WORKPLACE DISCRIMINATION BY EXISTING LAWS.

...TITLE VII DOES NOT PROHIBIT DISCRIMINATION BASED ON GENDER IDENTITY PER SE.

JEFF SESSIONS

alt: Two grayscale brush portraits of men in dark suits and ties side by side on a mottled dark gray background, the left one impassive, the right one grimacing with teeth showing. A magenta ribbon banner under each is lettered GORSUCH and KAVANAUGH, with hand-lettered white and magenta text above them.
text:
TRUMP HAS ALSO PACKED THE COURTS, INCLUDING THE SUPREME COURT, WITH CONSERVATIVE JUSTICES WHO COULD PREVENT PROGRESS AND ROLL BACK EXISTING PROTECTIONS.

GORSUCH
KAVANAUGH

alt: A large charcoal-and-magenta profile of Donald Trump fills the left half of a black square, his mouth open in mid-shout and his hair rendered in loose scribbled strokes. A magenta ribbon banner at the bottom is lettered TRUMP, and hand-lettered white and magenta text is stacked down the right side.
text:
THE SUPREME COURT WILL HEAR THE CASES THIS FALL . THE COURT'S RULINGS COULD COME OUT IN 2020, DURING AN ELECTION YEAR. TRUMP WILL LIKELY BE RUNNING FOR REELECTION AND TOUTING THE SAME ANTI-TRANS CRUELTY THAT HAS CHARACTERIZED HIS FIRST TERM.

TRUMP

alt: Two protesters against a pink wash: a Black woman in sunglasses and a magenta top raises a large hand-lettered sign overhead, and behind her a smiling woman with glasses and short hair holds another sign at chest height. Hand-lettered white and magenta text fills a pink band across the top of the panel.
text:
IT'S IMPORTANT FOR THOSE WHO SUPPORT LGBT EQUALITY TO TAKE ACTION NOW TO STOP DISCRIMINATION, INSTEAD OF WAITING FOR A SCOTUS RULING. WE CAN SUPPORT FEDERAL LEGISLATION SUCH AS THE EQUALITY ACT, RAISE AWARENESS OF EMPLOYMENT DISCRIMINATION AND PUSH OUR OWN COMPANIES AND STATES TO TAKE A STAND FOR JUSTICE.

TRANS RIGHTS ARE HUMAN RIGHTS!
STOP JOB DISCRIMINATION
